memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Now Moses said to Hobab son of Reuel the Midianite, Moses' father-in-law, "We are setting out for the place about which the Lord said, 'I will give it to you.' Come with us and we will treat you well, for the Lord has promised good things to Israel." He answered, "No, I will not go; I am going back to my own land and my own people." But Moses said, "Please do not leave us. You know where we should camp in the desert, and you can be our eyes." - Num 10:29-31 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses turns to his relative Hobab and warmly invites him: "Come with us... the Lord has promised good things to Israel." Hobab was not an Israelite, yet Moses longed for him to share in the journey and the blessing God had promised. When Hobab hesitated, Moses urged again: "Please do not leave us."

There is something moving about this. Moses did not want to keep the good things of God to himself and his own people. His heart reached out to include Hobab, to draw him along, to share the journey toward the promise. He genuinely wanted this outsider to belong.

This is the heart of a person who has tasted God's goodness — they want others to come along too. When we have experienced the grace and faithfulness of God, the natural response is to invite others to share in it. "Come with us," we say, "God is good, and there is room for you."

Moses also valued what Hobab could offer: "you can be our eyes." Hobab knew the desert well. Even as Moses invited him into blessing, he recognised the gift Hobab could bring. In God's family, welcoming others often means both blessing them and being blessed by them.

Who is God putting on your heart to invite along on the journey of faith? Like Moses, we can warmly say, "Come with us. God has been good to us, and He has room for you too." The invitation of the gospel is exactly this — a loving "come" to all who will hear (Matt 11:28).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you invite others to share in the goodness of God you've tasted?
- Who might God be putting on your heart to say "come with us" to?
- How can you both bless others and be blessed by them?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You for the good things You have given me in Christ. Give me Moses' heart to warmly invite others to come and share the journey with You. Amen.
